## H2 (content headline): the through-map predicted-answer similarity wins the change race

**Claim.** At per-prefix grain, P3b — cos(M0·c̄(P), A_ans): the destination prefix's context vector pushed through the base context→answer map, compared to the training-answer centroid — is the best pre-fine-tuning predictor of fine-tuning-induced leakage CHANGE (trained − base per-prefix graded score), dethroning the #1900 per-query change champion P2 (raw answer similarity).

- Across-arm median within-arm Spearman ρ: **P3b 0.411** vs P2 0.301, P10 (kNN answer-side) 0.325, P1 0.251, P6 0.288, P7 −0.113 (propensity is uninformative-to-negative for CHANGE).
- Winner probability (winner re-selected per draw): **0.655** prefix-resample PRIMARY, **0.806** query-cluster, **0.649** family-cluster. Selection-inherited CI on the winning median: [0.269, 0.557] (frozen-at-winner [0.232, 0.549], labeled). P3b beats P2 paired-within-arm in 9/12 content arms (the registered dethrone threshold).
- Permutation null (per-draw max over ~12 candidates): p97.5 ≈ 0.37–0.40 per arm — the pooled median 0.411 sits at/above the selected-max band; per-arm values clear it in the strong arms (e.g. casualness persona contrastive 0.658; impoliteness contrastive s42/s137 0.415/0.406 — the seed pair replicates).
- Figure: `figures/issue_1979/hero_content_race.png` (middle panel + winner bars); low-level per-unit view: `figures/issue_1979/scatter_imp-pers-con-lr3e5-s42.png` (per-prefix DV vs P7/P1/P2, family-colored, trained + negative prefixes labeled).

This is the verbatim user-roster predictor #3 ("context vector → apply mapping → predicted answer vector similarity"), which #1900 could not crown at per-query grain. **Alternatives considered:** (a) P3b's edge over P2 could be map-induced denoising (the ridge map contracts noise directions in c̄(P)) rather than structural mediation — partially countered by P3b also beating P3a (through-map context-anchor form, 0.214) and by the mediation lattice below; (b) P3b and P2 are highly rank-correlated (0.90 in the casualness arms) so the margin per arm is modest — the paired 9/12 + three consistent bootstrap families carry the claim; (c) one arm class (sycophancy positive-only) shows ≈ 0 for all change candidates (P3b −0.045) — its reliability ceiling is also the panel's lowest (√r_yy 0.587). Confidence: MODERATE.

## H4 battery

**A7 (whitened gate): still refuted — median ρ(g, matched-text write coefficient) = 0.175 over 36 content (arm × layer) cells; 38.9% in the registered [0.3, 0.7] band (needed: median in band AND ≥ 50% of cells).** The per-query anchor was 0.14, so prefix grain barely moves the pooled read. NEW structure the pooled criterion hides: the gate lands IN band for every positive-only content arm (impoliteness po L14/19/25 = 0.478/0.532/0.483; sycophancy po 0.483/0.442/0.468; casualness po 0.530/0.576/0.542) and for the casualness contrastive LoRA arm at L19 (0.477), while contrastive/FT/bare-trained arms sit near 0 (e.g. cas FT 0.073 at L19, imp FT 0.175). A plausible mechanism — the contrastive negatives train per-prefix writes DOWN exactly where the gate predicts them UP, distorting the gate correlation in con arms — is post-hoc; registered verdict stands. Figure: `figures/issue_1979/a7_gate.png`.

**A6 (write rank): still refuted at the registered 0.6 criterion (2/18 arms ≥ 0.6: casualness po 0.643, marker FT 0.605) — but the top-1 SVD share of the 50-prefix matched-text write matrix rises to median ≈ 0.43 (range 0.30–0.64) vs the per-query references 0.09 (matched) / 0.29 (on-policy).** Averaging over queries removes most query-idiosyncratic rank; the per-prefix write is far closer to rank-1 than the per-query read suggested, without reaching the panel-era 0.81–0.86. Rank ceiling: 50 rows ⇒ rank ≤ 50 by construction (registered line 8; top-1 SHARE is scale-free). On-policy-tree shares run lower (0.10–0.46). Figure: `figures/issue_1979/a6_top1_share.png`.

**A5 (write–delta alignment): the registered expectation "matched-text write–δ alignment stays null (text-carried)" is REFUTED — in both directions.** Pooled cos(matched-text write leg, on-policy delta leg; disjoint query halves) clears the corpus-covariance norm-matched null band (abs p95 0.03–0.43) in all 18 arms: casualness +0.35..+0.68 and impoliteness +0.51..+0.80 POSITIVE; **every marker arm strongly NEGATIVE (−0.63..−0.99)**; sycophancy mixed (conv-con −0.905, po −0.332, bare/ft +0.53/+0.64). Read-out alignment cos(write, r_B): impoliteness 0.30–0.48, casualness 0.19–0.43, sycophancy/marker ≈ 0 (−0.09..+0.04) — family-level as expected. The shared-B̄ pooled read (0.95) is record-only, known-invalid. Interpretation: at prefix grain the weights-carried write direction is systematically RELATED to the on-policy shift — same direction for the two style behaviors, opposite for the marker family (the on-policy delta includes emitted-marker token content the base-text teacher-forced write cannot contain; the sign structure is a real signature, mechanism unresolved). Figure: `figures/issue_1979/a5_alignment.png`. Confidence: MODERATE (sign structure is large and consistent within family; the leg construction differs from the per-query A5's δ = training-mix direction, so this is a re-operationalization, not a strict re-test — carry as scope note).

## H5: negatives sit below the geometry fit — but so do the placebos; suppression signature NOT demonstrated

The registered criterion technically PASSES: median signed residual of the 5 trained contrastive-negative prefixes vs the within-arm geometry fit is < 0 in 6/7 con content arms (0.857) and 4/4 con marker arms (1.0), i.e. `criterion_pass_2of3_both: true`, and `summary.json` labels H5 `H5-suppression-signature`. **The registered falsifier ALSO fires, and it controls:** the plan states "a residual < 0 that appears EQUALLY in po/bare arms is the generic low-elicitation-family artifact, not suppression," and the placebo arms are equally negative — casualness po −3.45 vs con −3.66 (bare placebo −5.75); impoliteness po −2.70 vs con −2.66/−4.11; marker po 0.00 vs con −0.03..−0.10 (trivial magnitudes, ≤ 0.1 nats); the con−po within-behavior median difference — the registered suppression signature — is ≈ 0 for three of four behaviors (cas −0.07, imp −0.01, mk −0.08) and −1.02 only for sycophancy (the lowest-reliability family, and its con arms are mixed: syc-conv +0.67). On the CHANGE DV the same picture holds (e.g. bare-placebo cas −5.59 vs con −0.63..−0.90 — the placebo is MORE negative).

**Honest verdict: geometry over-predicts leakage into the trained negative prefixes AND the placebo arms' negatives about equally — a generic property of that prefix family (all five negatives are assistant-adjacent, low-elicitation contexts), not evidence that contrastive training added prefix-selective suppression.** The `H5-suppression-signature` label in `summary.json` and the h5 figure title key only on the 2/3 criterion and should be corrected in the clean-result body (the per-arm JSON deliberately persists residuals so this regrouping is a pure re-read). Figure: `figures/issue_1979/h5_residuals.png` — the placebo (orange/green) diamonds visibly sit below zero alongside the con (blue) diamonds. Confidence in the corrected read: MODERATE (5 negatives per arm; medians over n=5).
